reasoning_summary: Setup matches the question. Re = 0.15*0.01/1.5e-5 = 100 and is configured as 100. The inlet is measured as uniform (ux_nonuniformity 0.0). The force reference uses magUInf 0.15, lRef 0.01, rhoInf 1.2, which is consistent with the stated fluid.

The domain is large for an 'unbounded' stream: 30D upstream, 50D downstream, 40D half-height, blockage 0.0125. Boundary conditions are sensible (fixedValue outlet pressure, inletOutlet outlet velocity, symmetry lateral boundaries). I cannot quantify the residual blockage effect from this evidence, which is a minor uncertainty against the 3% tolerance.

The numerics are adequate. The scheme is second-order (backward in time, linearUpwind). Max Courant is 0.73 with 0.01 convective-unit steps. About 614 steps per shedding period. Mass imbalance is 8.3e-11. checkMesh passes, with max non-orthogonality 43.3 deg and skewness 0.53. There are 160 cells around the cylinder and a first cell of 0.005D.

The submitted averaging window started at 0 and includes the start-up transient (transient end detected at 27.88 convective units). Its reported values are therefore contaminated, and its Strouhal frequency resolution (0.016669) is coarse. The stationary-window values are clean, taken over 5 cycles: Cd 1.3266 and St 0.163.

The stationary-window values are statistically stable. The Cd 95% CI is 0.0058 (about 0.44%). Drift is 1.04% and the half-window difference is 0.56%, all well under 3%. St from cycle counting (0.163) and from FFT (0.16316) agree. Rms lift 0.22362 is consistent with the Cl amplitude 0.31635 divided by sqrt(2).
The contaminated reported values (Cd 1.3196, St 0.16144) differ from the stationary ones by only about 0.5% and 1%, so the conclusion is robust to which window is used.

Remaining caveats: there is only one mesh and no refinement study, and the wake mesh is fairly coarse (last wake cell 1.02D, representative cell 0.457D). With internal consistency this good, I judge the quantities likely within 3%, but not with high confidence.
